name: manifest-dev
description: Manifest-driven development: /figure-out reaches shared understanding, /define writes Deliverables with Acceptance Criteria and Global Invariants, and /do implements them. Each gate is one text — a title, a body, and an optional why — carrying a required kind (judgment or deterministic, never inferred) as its only structured metadata; execution policy is selected at /do launch as per-gate (independent default), consolidated, or self, with an optional verifier model for independent modes. Every mode keeps a provenance-rich gate ledger and the run never downgrades itself. Re-verification follows each gate's declared kind: command-backed gates re-run in full, while judgment gates take one full look and then judge only prior findings' repairs and the changed delta, with --exhaustive-verification restoring full re-sampling. A default-on execution log preserves deviations and dead-end memory; --no-log opts out. For unattended runs, use a host-native goal-setting backstop whose completion contract requires fresh PASS evidence for every gate under the selected mode. /auto chains the full flow, and /figure-out-team extends deliberation to multi-party Slack sessions. /ticket-up splits a finished manifest into self-sufficient, implementer-agnostic tickets with dependency edges — each shaped only when no open question would change what gets built or what done means, and each judged at emit for the opt-in Auto grant that alone lets unattended automation take a ticket end to end, absence keeping automation off it entirely, and each carrying an optional single type naming what kind of work it is (bug, feature, refactor, docs, chore by default, replaceable per project) so an automation rollout widens by editing a query rather than re-deciding the grant ticket by ticket, an untyped ticket being passed over by anything selecting on type — the project's shared tracker recommended, GitHub Issues out of the box, files in-repo where there is no tracker, and an unmapped tracker gets a venue reference written from the user's answers, on a venue asked once per project and recorded there — and /next-ticket pulls the top ready ticket back out with its reason and claims it, so parallel sessions each get a different one. /init-context sets a repository up with the surfaces the workflow reads from — project-owned ADR conventions, a glossary, and the context-file wiring that keeps sessions using them — seeding them from the project's own history where there is any.
